## Key Takeaways


- Improving mobility in Bakersfield requires a coordinated program, as shown by the Thomas Roads Improvement Program (TRIP) involving 24 projects over 20 years.
- TRIP, led by various local and federal agencies, aims to enhance safety, connectivity, and operational efficiency in the transportation network.
- Parsons managed all project phases, including planning, design management, and environmental compliance, ensuring smooth project delivery.
- Key projects include the SR 178/Fairfax Road Interchange and SR 58 Gap Closure, which improve regional traffic flow and capacity.
- TRIP enhances community character with aesthetic infrastructure designs and serves as a commitment to long-term mobility and economic vitality in Bakersfield.


**Improving mobility across a growing metropolitan region requires more than delivering individual roadway projects.** It demands a coordinated program that integrates planning, funding, environmental compliance, design, construction, grant, and stakeholder collaboration. The Thomas Roads Improvement Program (TRIP) exemplified that approach, advancing a comprehensive portfolio of transportation improvements throughout metropolitan Bakersfield.


Led by the City of Bakersfield (the City) in partnership with Caltrans, Kern County, the Kern Council of Governments (KernCOG), and the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), TRIP comprised 24 projects planned over a 20-year period. By summer 2026, 23 projects had been completed, one recently opened, and one remained in planning.


Since 2006, Parsons served as a trusted delivery partner, providing comprehensive program management, technical oversight, environmental support, design management, and construction services that helped transform a long-range vision into a coordinated network of transportation improvements.


### Managing a Complex Program from Planning Through Construction


We have supported nearly every phase of project delivery, providing program and project management, project controls, document management, environmental compliance, permitting, field monitoring, corridor planning, concept development, and project scoping. Our team also managed consultant contracts on behalf of the City, performed design reviews, evaluated alternative delivery approaches, and provided both technical and management resources throughout project development and construction, along with funding, financial, and grant support services.


This integrated approach enabled the City to efficiently advance projects through complex environmental, technical, regulatory, and administrative processes while maintaining program objectives and schedules.


### Delivering Critical Transportation Improvements


TRIP included a diverse range of projects designed to enhance mobility, safety, connectivity, and operational efficiency across Bakersfield’s transportation network.


One of the program’s earliest construction efforts was the $29 million SR 178/Fairfax Road Interchange Project. Our team provided construction management and construction engineering inspection services for the extension of SR 178 to Caltrans freeway standards.


For the SR 58 Gap Closure Project, we supported improvements that widened the freeway from four to six lanes between Hughes Lane and Cottonwood Road. By constructing the additional lanes within the existing median, the project created a continuous six-lane facility between SR 99 and SR 184, improving regional traffic flow and operational efficiency.


The Rosedale Highway Widening Project improved traffic circulation and travel times by expanding the corridor to three lanes in each direction. Additional improvements were delivered at the SR 99/Rosedale Highway Interchange, where the southbound off-ramp was expanded from a single-lane exit to a two-lane exit with four lanes at the intersection. Our team obtained project approvals, prepared environmental documentation, completed roadway and retaining-wall design, coordinated utility relocations, and supported easement acquisition efforts.


### Advancing Multimodal Mobility and Safety


TRIP’s benefits extended beyond highway capacity improvements. The award-winning SR-43 (Enos Lane)/Stockdale Highway Roundabout Project enhanced mobility and safety for drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists by replacing a traditional four-way stop with a modern roundabout.


The project included roadway reconstruction, landscaping, utility relocations, drainage improvements, retaining walls, ADA-compliant pedestrian facilities, bicycle lanes, and right-of-way acquisition. We provided overall project management, preliminary engineering, project report development, environmental clearance, and final design services.


To accommodate future growth, the roundabout was designed with the flexibility to operate initially as a single-lane facility while allowing expansion to two lanes as traffic demands increase.


## Enhancing Community Character Through Infrastructure


In addition to transportation improvements, we helped integrate landscape architecture and aesthetics throughout the TRIP program and related corridor projects.


At the SR-99/Hosking Avenue Interchange, we developed final landscape and irrigation designs incorporating Blue Palo Verde trees, drought-tolerant planting palettes, decorative stone treatments, and enhanced hardscape features. Similar efforts were implemented along the Westside Parkway and the SR-58/99 Interchange, where landscape improvements, monuments, and public-art elements were incorporated to strengthen community identity and create distinctive gateway features.


These enhancements contributed to a transportation network that not only improves mobility but also reflects the character and identity of Bakersfield.


### Delivering Long-Term Regional Benefits


The eight phases of the Centennial Corridor Project (State Route 58 Gap Closure) was the cornerstone element of Bakersfield’s long-range Thomas Roads Improvement Program, providing a new controlled-access freeway connection between State Route 58, Westside Parkway, and the regional highway network.


The project eliminated a long-standing gap in the east-west transportation corridor through metropolitan Bakersfield by constructing approximately 1.7 miles of new freeway, major system and local interchanges, braided ramp connections, grade separations, retaining walls, drainage infrastructure, utility relocations, and extensive roadway reconstruction.


The Thomas Roads Improvement Program demonstrates how a coordinated, long-term investment strategy can successfully address the transportation needs of a growing metropolitan area. Through environmental planning, funding support, design management, construction management, and stakeholder coordination, we helped the City of Bakersfield advance projects from concept through completion.


With 23 projects completed, two under construction, and one awaiting funding as of summer 2022, TRIP represents a sustained commitment to improving mobility, safety, connectivity, and quality of life for the Bakersfield community.


Through collaboration among public agencies, project partners, and our team, the program transformed a collection of individual projects into a unified transportation initiative that continues to support the region’s long-term growth and economic vitality.
